metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Panama

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive international comparisons for Panama using the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment administered to 15-year-olds across participating countries and economies. The excerpt does not specify whether student/sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in the production of the reported means, percentages, and correlations, nor does it name any weight variables. For PISA analyses, analysts should use the official PISA sampling weights (and replicate weights if variance estimation is required) from the OECD PISA database to account for the complex two-stage sampling of students within schools and the stratified design. Because the factsheet is a secondary reporting product and the methodology details are not included here, the exact weighting and variance-estimation approach cannot be verified from the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The provided factsheet excerpt does not describe any student-level predictive modeling or the use of PV-based achievement scores; it reports proficiency summaries, proficiency-level shares, and descriptive relationships (e.g., correlations and variance explained) for creative thinking. As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable to the extraction target here, and the excerpt also does not document any missing-data strategy for the reported estimates. This is best interpreted as a reporting gap in the excerpt rather than evidence that missing data were absent.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for Panama consists of 4,544 students in 215 schools who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, and for whom creative thinking results are reported in this factsheet. The excerpt does not specify additional exclusions (e.g., missing background questionnaire items) or any further task-level completion filters beyond the stated completion of the assessment.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Panama’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment includes 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. In Panama, the mean creative thinking score is 23 on a 60-point scale, which is significantly below the OECD average (33). About 47% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), and 7% are top performers at Levels 5–6. The factsheet also reports that socio-economic status is a strong predictor of creative thinking in Panama (explaining 14% of variation), and that creative thinking is positively correlated with mathematics (0.64) and reading (0.66). Interpretation should consider PISA’s technical standards and the note that some countries/economies may have sampling-standard limitations (asterisks), while this excerpt does not provide the underlying variance-estimation and missing-data procedures.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 factsheet that reports descriptive results and international comparisons rather than an original empirical study that trains and evaluates machine learning models. Consequently, there are no ML techniques, no predictive targets, and no model performance metrics to extract, and the main_findings table is intentionally empty. The excerpt also does not provide the technical details needed to document PV handling and missing-data procedures for any inferential modeling beyond the published PISA reporting.
